newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Hesse-Bonn gold plan seen as "creative".
newsitem.headline: Buba's Hesse-Bonn gold plan seen as "creative".

text.p: A senior Bundesbank official on Monday said that the Bonn government's plans to plug fiscal holes by revaluing reserves would be tantamount to creative accounting.

"A transfer of funds in 1997 would be comparable to creative accounting," Bundesbank central council member Helmut Hesse said using the same words used by his colleague Otmar Issing to describe the Bonn government's plans to revalue German gold and currency assets.
Hesse added that if a transfer were to occur this year, there would be a considerable danger that the trust in the future common currency's stability could be eroded.
Hesse who is also the president of the state central bank in Lower Saxony, Saxony Anhalt and Bremen made the remarks in a prepared speech.

He said he wished that Germany's parliament could still find another way out of its fiscal crisis without resorting to asking to receive a portion of the profits from an immediate revaluation of reserves.
A transfer of unrealised profits could be seen to undermine the credibility of stability oriented policies, Hesse said.
